Multimodal Large Language Models have achieved impressive performances in mathematical reasoning, yet they remain vulnerable to visual hallucinations and logical inconsistencies that standard outcome-based supervision fails to mitigate. **Two-Stage RL Training Framework:**
A two-stage RL training framework has been proposed to first enhance visual perception of geometric structures, then foster reasoning capabilities. Limitations in vision-intensive reasoning benchmarks often originate from foundational issues in visual understanding, as fundamental errors in vision understanding affect subsequent logical deductions and prevent the model from being rewarded during RL training.

## HERMES Framework

HERMES performs intermediate formal checking to prevent reasoning drift and employs a memory module that maintains proof continuity across long, multi-step reasoning chains, enabling both exploration and verification within a single workflow.

The framework was evaluated on four challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks using LLMs of varying parameter scales, and across all settings, Hermes reliably improves the reasoning accuracy of base models while substantially reducing token usage and computational cost compared to reward-based approaches.

On difficult datasets such as AIME'25, Hermes achieves up to a 67% accuracy improvement while using 80% fewer total inference FLOPs.

## Related Trends in Reinforcement Learning with Verification

The search results also reveal broader trends in this space. Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has recently demonstrated notable success in enhancing the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), particularly in mathematics and programming tasks.

Methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) leverage strictly binary, programmatically verifiable rewards—such as test-passing in code or exact equivalence in mathematics—to achieve robust, theoretically guaranteed success amplification.

## Overview

Qwen3-VL is the most powerful vision-language model in the Qwen series to date. It's a multimodal large language model series developed by Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud.

This generation delivers comprehensive upgrades across the board: superior text understanding & generation, deeper visual perception & reasoning, extended context length.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about LeanGeo:

## Overview

LeanGeo is a unified formal system for formalizing and solving competition-level geometry problems within the Lean 4 theorem prover. It features a comprehensive library of high-level geometric theorems with Lean's foundational logic, enabling rigorous proof verification and seamless integration with Mathlib.

## Key Components

The core of LeanGeo is its theorem library, comprising 260 manually written, formally proved, and auto-verified geometric theorems. It builds upon the axiomatic framework of SystemE (Avigad et al., 2009) and extends LeanEuclid (Murphy et al., 2024).

## LeanGeo-Bench Benchmark

LeanGeo-Bench comprises 122 geometry problems, including all International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) geometry problems since 2000. The project presents 43 formally verified solutions to problems in the benchmark, including two from the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), all of which are machine-checked in Lean.

## Training and Evaluation

The framework proposes a training methodology that uses the theorem library to construct supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data, which is then used in reinforcement learning (RL) experiments upon the Kimi k1.5 reinforcement learning pipeline, yielding promising initial results.
